speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: asked the Minister for Education (Schools) (a) what is the current capacity and take-up rate of after-school student care centres; (b) how does the Ministry continuously ensure that student care remains affordable; and (c) whether there are plans to set minimum operating standards for after-school care.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: There are also SCCs outside of schools that provide after-school care for students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Together, MOE and MSF monitor the capacities and enrolment of both school-based and community-based SCCs closely.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: MSF regularly reviews the ComCare SCFA scheme to ensure that student care remains affordable for lower-income families.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: All registered SCCs are required to comply with requirements covering areas like supervision, safety, health and hygiene.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: In addition, for school-based SCCs, the service providers are selected via a stringent and competitive procurement process and have to meet contractual requirements for quality in areas, such as programmes, staff training, level of care and environment.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Schools maintain close oversight of SCC operations to ensure that quality is maintained.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Speaker, I would like to thank the Minister for his comprehensive reply.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: There has been feedback from parents, especially in schools whereby there are younger parents and more children, that some schools have to prioritise the after-school student care for the lower primary students.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: This has caused some inconvenience, especially when they have two or more children in school and one of them has to go into the private space.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Can I check with the Minister if the plan is to cater capacity for all levels of primary school students?

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: The size of the waitlist for primary schools varies for different schools.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: But on average, the number of waitlisted students is low.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Where there is excess demand, schools will work with the SCC operators to see how we can expand the number of classrooms to cater for this enrolment demand.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Having said that, it is with the caveat that this expansion does not compromise the quality of student care.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: As I have said in the reply earlier, MOE has expanded the student care facilities quite tremendously in the last few years.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, while we cater to the quantity of students needing the care, we want to ensure that the quality is built up correspondingly as well.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: In the midst of building up these student care centres, we ensure the quality and, therefore, the overall standards, whether it is environment, hygiene, even some of the programmes.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: With these training programmes, we hope to uplift and upkeep standards.
